question.:question/problem: Given that $w(x,y,z)=x{z}^{4}+y,$ find $\frac{∂w}{∂r},$ where $(x,y,z)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the corresponding cylindrical polar coordinates.

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂r} & =({z}^{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={z}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
